subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Outdoor, Adventure, and Community Recreation Planning

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of planning a longer or more demanding outdoor activity in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe risk assessment for an unfamiliar environment using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply navigation, communication, and contingency planning in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving group planning and shared responsibility; correct it and explain why.
Connect cost, transport, permits, and access realities with environmental stewardship and shared-space responsibility and explain how one affects the other.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Produce a complete plan for one guardian-approved outdoor or community activity — risk assessment, logistics, contingency, and stewardship — and carry it out if approved, or complete the equivalent local or indoor version.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Outdoor, Adventure, and Community Recreation Planning?
